text: Too much beer, and a man's heart will be open for all to see
source: The Saga of Olaf Haraldsson, c.151

text: The error is the result of letting fear rule your actions
source: The Saga of Harald Hardrade, c.46

text: A person should not agree today to what he will regret tomorrow
Defend your own judgment and not what others say
No one is a fool if he knows when to shut up
Not all the clouds that darken the day bring rain
It is better to fight and fall than to live without hope
source: The Saga of the Volsungs, c.12

text: Where the wolf's ears are, the wolf's teeth are close.
Fight your enemies in the field, don't burn in your home
When men encounter enemies in the fight, a robust heart is better than a sharp sword
Only a coward expects to be taken as a redfish or a fox from a trap
We often regret saying too much and seldom regret saying too little
source: The saga of Hrafnkel Freysgothi, c.7

text: Those who take large resolutions, and then set them aside, only end in disgrace
source: The saga of King Olaf Trygvisson, c.9

text: Gold is little comfort to the dead relative
The one you trust the most may disappoint you the most
Ill is the result of letting fear rule thine actions
source: The Saga of Harald Hardrade, c.46

text: Ill it is to take love from another man’s wife
Kinsmen to kinsmen should be true.
source: The Saga of Olaf Haraldsson, c.186

text: Fear not death for the hour of your doom is set and none may escape it
Often times it is not numbers that wins the victory, but those who fare forward with the most vigor
source: The Saga of Thrond of Gate, c.19

text: With many who come to power and honor, pride keeps pace with promotion
source: The Saga of Magnus the Good, c.8

text: Ill it is to abandon honor and integrity in exchange for injustice and greed
There is more honor in accumulating little by little than in reaching for the sky and ending up flat on your face
A person’s actions are often worse than their intentions
source: The Saga of Hrafnkel Freysgothi, c.10

text: Stubbornness brings either greater humiliation or greater honor
source: The Saga of Hrafnkel Freysgothi, c.10

text: When truth and fairness are different from what is law, better it is to follow truth and fairness
Wisdom is welcome wherever it comes from
Great deeds and ill deeds often fall within each other’s shadow
Better to die with honor than live with shame
source: The Saga of the Jomsvikings, c.23

text: Oft one finds, when the foe he meets, that he is not the bravest of all
All a people need in order to rise up against tyranny is a leader bold enough to take up the banner
source: The Saga of Harald Hardrade, c.45

text: That which has a bad beginning, is likely to have a bad ending
One should not ask more than would be thought fitting
Often it is that what happens to most others will happen to you
Better a brief spell of honour than a long rule of shame
There is greater consolation than money
He’s a wise man who knows himself
source: The Saga of Hrafnkel Freysgothi, c.7

text: Let another’s wounds be your warning
Bravery is half the victory
source: The Saga of Harald Hardrade, c.103

text: A hungry wolf is bound to wage a hard battle
The fool is busy in everyone’s business but his own
Often it is that anger is blind to the truth
Better it is to have a lower position in life and be free than to have a position of power only to be subject to the will of another
source: The Saga of Olaf Haraldsson, c.79

text: Ill is the result of being more given to big talk than using one’s wits
source: The Saga of Bjarn of the Hitdoela Champions, c.19

text: With law shall our land be built up and settled, and with lawlessness wasted and spoiled
It can be expected that a man who has a lot on his mind will not always be careful enough
source: The Saga of Hrafnkel Freysgothi, c.9

text: Where fault can be found, the good is ignored
A tale is but half told when only one person tells it
